profile.goal: No goal race - open-ended base building. Run farther and faster while feeling strong, lower average HR (aerobic efficiency + resting HR trend), build muscle, ride bike opportunistically.
profile.rest_day_policy: No fixed rest day - readiness (sleep/HRV/RHR/Body Battery/Garmin composite scores) decides day to day
profile.gym_split: 3x/week: Chest/Tri early week, Back/Bi later week, Legs on Sunday
profile.bike_policy: Flexible/ad hoc, roughly 1x/week, used when running isn't the right call that day - not a fixed training pillar
profile.known_issue: Three straight easy-day HR overshoots (07-14, 07-17, 07-19) all happened on trail/hilly routes. Garmin's own Training Status flagged 'Unproductive - Low Aerobic Shortage' over the trailing 4 weeks, corroborating this independently. This week's easy days are deliberately routed flat/road to isolate terrain as a variable - but see heat_context below, which arrived after the initial version of this plan and is likely also a real contributor to elevated HR.
profile.heat_context: Little Rock under an Extreme Heat Warning through Tue 07-21 evening: highs ~100F, heat index 105-115F, overnight lows stuck in the 80s (source: NWS / arkansasonline.com, checked 2026-07-20). A cooler front arrives Wed but highs stay mid-upper 90s through at least Thu. Poor overnight cooling likely contributes to Garmin's 'High Recovery Need' reading independent of training discipline. HR targets are loosened and outdoor running is paused on the peak-danger day (Tue) as a result.
